messages:
maria.k: quick heads-up — onboarding `open-embed-xl` quantized with `q4_0` shows a sharp drop in recall@5 on RQA-1k compared to float32. baseline (redwood-embed-v2 fp32) recall@5=0.87, q4_0 recall@5=0.69 :thinking:
aj: can you paste the full eval table and exact configs?
sasha: Oof that's big. any change to tokenization or preproc?
maria.k: nothing changed in preproc. same tokenizer, same indexing. ran 3 seeds. full summary: 
- dataset: rqa-1k (hard negatives)
- metric: recall@1/5/10 + mean reciprocal rank (mrr)
- baseline redwood-embed-v2 fp32: recall@1=0.62, recall@5=0.87, recall@10=0.91, mrr=0.69
- open-embed-xl fp32: recall@1=0.60, recall@5=0.86, recall@10=0.90, mrr=0.68
- open-embed-xl q4_0 (GPTQ-like): recall@1=0.44, recall@5=0.69, recall@10=0.78, mrr=0.52
- open-embed-xl q8_0 (8-bit): recall@5=0.83 (pretty close)
- clustering (kmeans 50) silhouette: fp32=0.38, q4_0=0.21

samir: so 4-bit is the culprit here. curious if cosine vs dot changed ranking?
maria.k: used cosine for all. i also re-ran with dot — relative drop persists but magnitudes shift (dot slightly better for q4_0 but still ~0.72 recall@5 vs 0.86 fp32).
aj: possible causes: weight ordering mismatch in GPTQ export, KV cache quant mismatch (though embeddings shouldn't use cache), or activation folding differences. did you try the straight quantization script vs our optimized quant pack?
maria.k: tried both. `quantize.py --mode gptq` and `quant_pack_v2`. both show large drop. i ran per-layer bias correction for gptq too, no dice.
sasha: can you run a small diagnostic — nearest neighbor distances for a set of 100 anchors, compare rank positions between fp32 and q4_0, and dump top 10 ids for a couple of examples?
maria.k: yes doing that now. quick sample: anchor id 123 -> fp32 top5 [512, 98, 77, 44, 3], q4_0 top5 [98, 77, 512, 901, 44] — ordering changed a bit, but for many anchors true positive moves out of top5 completely.
eval-bot: eval run finished. attached metrics: recall@1:0.44, recall@5:0.69, recall@10:0.78, mrr:0.52 (consistent)
aj: can you share the exact export command + git hash? also which quant backend? cuBLAS or XPU?
maria.k: export command: ```
python scripts/quantize.py --model open-embed-xl --bits 4 --backend gptq --calib-samples 2000 --out artifacts/open-embed-xl-q4
```
commit: `a7d3f9c` (model-team/open-embeds)

samir: let's also sanity-check with evaluation on semantic-sim-50k and a small MS-MARCO subset. if it's only RQA failing maybe it's dataset sensitivity.
maria.k: ran semantic-sim-50k quick: fp32 recall@5=0.92, q4_0 recall@5=0.89 (small drop). MS-MARCO-1k: fp32=0.78, q4_0=0.60 (large). suggests quantization amplifies harder negative cases.
sasha: that pattern points to small-angle distortions in embedding space that break fine-grained nearest neighbor ordering. could be scale mismatches — check per-dim variance before/after quant.
maria.k: per-dim std ratio (q4_0 / fp32) avg=0.96 but tail dims compress a lot; top 5% dims variance reduced by ~30%.
aj: try symmetric rescaling per-dim (learned scale) before quant and dequant. also try OPQ (rotated quant) if available.
sasha: another ablation — quantize only the projection layers (final linear) and keep transformer in fp32, see how much loss we get.
maria.k: queued experiments: 1) per-dim scale + gptq 2) OPQ + gptq 3) quantize only final projection 4) run GPTQ with larger calib (10k samples)
eval-bot: benchmark runner note: increased calib >5k will add ~3h to pipeline.
maria.k: ack. starting 1) and 3) now. will post updates.

--- 45m later ---
maria.k: quick interim: quantize-final-proj-only yields recall@5=0.85 (almost baseline). so most of the hit came from earlier layers.
aj: interesting — that suggests cumulative quant noise across layers. try block-wise quantization with per-block scale.
samir: if final projection-only works well, running a hybrid—transformer at 8-bit, proj at 4-bit—might hit an acceptable perf/cost tradeoff. can we prototype latency for that on dedicated?
maria.k: sampled latency on ded1 (A100) with mixed q: throughput +18% vs fp32 and token latency +5ms. cost estimate reduction ~28% vs fp32.
sasha: for release checklist: 1) rerun full eval (rqa/msmarco/semantic-sim) on chosen hybrid config 2) add regression test to CI linking recall@k thresholds 3) document quant config and calibration samples 4) flag models that fail regression for dev review
maria.k: agreed. assigning: aj - investigate OPQ implementation; samir - run per-block quant with larger calib; sasha - add CI regression test template; i'll rerun full eval once hybrid is baked.
aj: starting OPQ PR today.
samir: kicking off 10k calib job now.
sasha: PR for CI test skeleton in a few hrs.
deploy-bot: canary deploy of quant-pipeline image `quant-runner:2026-03-20` started on eng-ml-nodes
maria.k: thanks all. folder: /mnt/artifacts/open-embed-xl/q4_troubleshoot contains dumps and NN lists. ping me for access.
aj: one more ask — can we capture a handful of failure cases (query + positive + negatives) to use for human eval? i'll take the labeling if you dump them.
maria.k: done, `artifacts/failure-cases-42.jsonl` uploaded. includes 150 cases with context.
sasha: good job triaging. follow-up sync tomorrow 11am to decide hybrid vs 8-bit default. :thumbsup:
aj: thx, see you 11am.
samir: noted.
